The local space $W_K$ therefore contains a basis flux with nonzero total outward flux, so $D_K:W_K\to\mathbb R$, $D_Kv=\int_K\operatorname{div}v$, is onto. The facet-multiplier terms cancel by normal continuity; the constant pressure term contributes $-c\int_D\operatorname{div}v_h=0$ by [F7]. The remaining equation is $a(u_h,v_h)-\int_D\bar p\operatorname{div}v_h=0$. Thus $(u_h,\bar p)$ is the conforming mixed solution, which is unique by [F3].

The map $J$ is onto: for each interior facet $F$, use [F5] on one adjacent cell with zero flux on its other facets and zero field on all other cells; its image is the coordinate vector for $F$. Substitution into $J_F(u)=0$ gives a linear system solely on the finitely many interior-facet multipliers; this is static condensation. Existence and correspondence follow from steps 1.1–2.2. Uniqueness [F3] forces $u=0$ and $p_K=c$ for one global constant. The local equations then read $\sum_{F\subset\partial K,\ F\mathrm{interior}}(\lambda_F-c)\int_Fv_K\cdot n_K=0$ for all $v_K\in W_K$, since Gauss–Green and the zero physical-boundary flux give $D_Kv_K=\sum_{F\mathrm{interior}}\int_Fv_K\cdot n_K$.
